system.summary: Maisse's Cipher (1592-1593), the key Henri IV also sent to Savary de Breves: letter-shaped symbols for the letters, homophonic, with two-digit figures for a nomenclator of common words and names.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction 'Maisse' Cipher 2 (BnF fr.16093, f.344 etc.)' (henryiv_Maisse2.png), in hand, not applied; ff. 398, 401, 402, 404 of the same volume carry partial interlinear decipherments
system.notes: Word codes on Tomokiyo's table include vous, ceulx, est, faict, de, des, fort, par, pour, que, qui, advis, ces, comme, bon, avec, et, jay, les, luy, moy. f. 404 says in clear that Maisse kept 'le double du chiffre que j'ay envoye aud. de Breves'. Commonest figures on f. 404: 27, 10, 26, 23, 19, 21, 22, 24, 8.

prior_solution.where: contemporary clear copies of both letters in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984) fol. 171r and 193v; f. 406's twin f. 404 carries a partial interlinear decipherment; Tomokiyo's key for the cipher published as an image on cryptiana; no reading of ff. 406/410 published

conditions.human_role: Project-level only: the target was taken from the repository's catalogue and worked by the model in Claude Code; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's Henri IV page re-read as HTML rather than as the text dump in research/gallica_sweep/src: the four leaves fall in two different cipher sections, each with siblings in the same volume, so the entry's class B and 'no sibling found' were both wrong.
fr. 16093 resolved to ark btv1b90074656 by Gallica SRU and the folio-to-canvas offsets calibrated by reading folio numbers off the leaves.

The old Harlay piece numbers 247 (f. 406) and 251 (f. 410) matched to Berger de Xivrey's citations, which give clear copies in fonds Brienne 13 = NAF 6984 (fol. 171r, 193v); located on the images by heading and preamble.
Tomokiyo's key image for this cipher (henryiv_Maisse2.png, 'Maisse' Cipher 2 (BnF fr.16093, f.344 etc.)') fetched from his page; not applied to ff. 406/410.

ff. 406 and 410 read from the Brienne clear copies; f. 406 shown to be the duplicate of f. 404 (same date, same opening, one Brienne copy), so its text is also attested by f. 404's interlinear decipherment; f. 412 is the duplicate of f. 410.

Novelty re-examined after Lasry's note on 'undeciphered'. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The page no longer says Tomokiyo 'never applied' his keys; the claim is a published reading only.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from maisse1592, which had joined ff. 370/373 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592) with ff. 406/410 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592-93, the Breves cipher). This profile keeps ff. 406 and 410 (Maisse's Cipher of 1592-93) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): no transcription or decryption of ff. 406/410 exists in the repository (the text was read from the Brienne 13 clear copies, not transcribed); entries link the Gallica images of the cipher leaves (and twin f. 404) and of the Brienne copies.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): no text of f. 406 or f. 410 is in the repository (images and links only). Both relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read; method read from existing decipherment -> not solved, until the Brienne 13 copies are transcribed.
Consistency pass (cl): documents[].read for f406, f410 read -> not read, matching outcome.texts (decoded, not read) and fraction_read_source.

WAINUT contribution: Brienne 13 (NAF 6984, btv1b100904592) canvases 176-178, 199-200 and the cipher leaves fr. 16093 (btv1b90074656) canvases 455, 457, 458, 461 viewed at full resolution (Gallica viewer and the BnF IIIF API at openapi.bnf.fr); no image kept in the repository.

WAINUT contribution: the clear copies transcribed line by line: fol. 171r (lower part) to 172v for f. 406 (wainut/f406_brienne_copy.txt) and fol. 193v, 194r and the first lines of 194v for f. 410 (wainut/f410_brienne_copy.txt). fol. 173r and the rest of 194v are not transcribed. The top of fol. 171r ('insollence des Espagnolz ... prier Dieu, etc.') was found to be the end of Maisse's own letter 'Au Roy du dixiesme Avril 1593' (heading on fol. 170v), not part of the King's letter of 8 Feb.

WAINUT contribution: the start of each cipher block fixed against the copies (f. 406 and twin f. 404: 'Le surplus de voz lettres ...', right after 'vous y pouvez apporter', on the same line of the leaf; f. 410: 'L'experience a faict cognoistre ...', after 'de ma bonne grace et faveur'). Six stretches (f. 410 cipher ll. 1-2, f. 404 l. 3, f. 406 cipher l. 1 and two pieces of l. 2; 128 signs) transcribed sign by sign (wainut/cipher_lines.txt) and decrypted with Tomokiyo's 'Maisse' Cipher 2' unchanged: they give the copy's text (wainut/f406_decryption.md, f410_decryption.md). Word signs 15 = faict, 17 = vous, 18 = est confirmed.

WAINUT contribution: wainut/decode_check.py: difflib ratio of decryption to copy 0.79-1.00 on the six stretches (0.91-0.94 on the three longest, 25-39 signs; 0.79 on the 13-sign stretch with two holes); 2000 random permutations of the key values give at most 0.67 on any stretch and 0.53 on the four longest; 2000 shuffles of the group order at most 0.65 on the three longest and 0.71 on the 13-sign stretch.

WAINUT contribution: a second, independent look at the images corrected the first sign-level alignment: on f. 404 the '9' is the uy sign (u) and the '+' the theta-like d; on f. 410 '9t' is c (not n), 's-long + hook' is two signs (e, n) and the z-like sign is a; the hooked q-like sign for l is in Tomokiyo's l column (not a new homophone); the cipher spells 'cougnoistre' and 'que vous en avez'; the copy has 'vous estes estes'. Still open: three signs where the copy has 'vous ne' decode r u e; the pi-like sign in 'Rome' and the '+' in 'voiage' do not fit the key.

texts.label: f. 406 (twin f. 404), Chartres, 8 Feb 1593 (not transcribed; images only)
texts.summary: Henri IV to Maisse at Venice: the King has answered every despatch and docketed the dates so Maisse can tell what is lost; the Spanish insolence and the Pope; Pisany and Cardinal Gondi should not leave Rome, since their entry among those of the League could breed division. The leaf, its twin f. 404 (partial interlinear decipherment) and the Brienne 13 fol. 171r clear copy are not transcribed in this repository; the links are to the Gallica images.
texts.note: Not in the repository: the content was read from the contemporary clear copy in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984, fol. 171r, canvas 176), which was never transcribed, and the cipher leaf itself was not deciphered; nothing of the letter is here (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: fetch the Brienne 13 page and the cipher leaf through the Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr) and transcribe the copy.

texts.label: f. 410 (twin f. 412), Mantes, 27 Apr 1593 (not transcribed; images only)
texts.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letters of 20 Feb, 7 and 23 Mar, notes that the duc de Nevers held one courier in Champagne, assures Maisse that his absence will cost him nothing in the King's favour, and says experience has proved his long-standing judgement of the affairs of Rome right. Neither the leaf nor its Brienne 13 fol. 193v clear copy is transcribed in this repository; the links are to the Gallica images.
texts.note: Not in the repository: the content was read from the contemporary clear copy in Brienne 13 (NAF 6984, fol. 193v, canvas 199), which was never transcribed, and the cipher leaf itself was not deciphered; nothing of the letter is here (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: fetch the Brienne 13 page and the cipher leaf through the Gallica IIIF (openapi.bnf.fr) and transcribe the copy.

texts.label: WAINUT, 27 Oct 2026: f. 406 (twin f. 404), Chartres, 8 Feb 1593, from the Brienne 13 clear copy; cipher decrypted on its first lines
texts.summary: Henri IV to Maisse at Venice: he has answered every despatch and noted their dates, approves Maisse's sending of duplicates, hopes the despatch for the Pope was not delayed, and has written to the Grand Seigneur and his ministers (Maisse can read the letter to Breves if he kept the copy of the cipher). From the start of the cipher block on (its end is not fixed): Rome; Pisany's arrival in Italy; the war in Piedmont and a letter sent through Lesdiguieres' men with a further charge for Lesdiguieres; Gondi at Nancy with the King's passport; the King going down to Saumur, where his sister is. The repository's earlier summary of f. 406 (the Spanish insolence, Pisany and Cardinal Gondi not to leave Rome) describes the top of fol. 171r, which is the end of Maisse's own letter to the King of 10 Apr 1593.

texts.label: WAINUT, 27 Oct 2026: f. 410 (twin f. 412), Mantes, 27/28 Apr 1593, from the Brienne 13 clear copy; cipher decrypted on its first two lines
texts.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letters of 20 Feb, 7 and 23 Mar (one courier held by the duc de Nevers in Champagne) and assures him that his absence will cost him nothing. In cipher: experience has proved Maisse right about the affairs of Rome; on advice the King will not yet recall Cardinal de Gondi or the marquis de Pisany, to keep the Pope from extremes, and leaves their moves to the Grand Duke's advice; Gondi's promises. Then (whether still in cipher is not fixed): the original letters of the Grand Seigneur and his ministers received; the King waits on the ambassador's despatch.
